findings.reason: the justification is the only thing standing between the deliverable and the same defect in a sibling guarded key, so a worker implementing §8 as written leaves the class half-fixed and the case list would need a `changed_paths` case added.
findings.text: §8 limits the whitespace-split to `test_logs` and justifies excluding the other guarded fields with "because `commits` entries are written as a sha followed by a subject", but `_GUARDED_LIST_KEYS` (reckon/crew/reports.py:115–117) is `{changed_paths, orientation_write_paths, test_logs, commits}`; `changed_paths` entries are paths, not sha-plus-subject, so a space-joined `changed_paths` line is read as one entry and every consumer that takes its entries one at a time — the same guard shape the section exists to repair — reads only the first path, while the stated reason appears to have cleared it

findings.reason: the third deliverable and its sixth case are still reachable and still worth building (a parseable no-arms manifest reaches it), so the node's work is unchanged; only the Why's attribution to the glued manifest is loose.
findings.text: §8's third deliverable is presented as the repair for the second cited defect ("the refusal … never says … nor where one was found"), but after the second deliverable lands the glued manifest is refused earlier and louder by `_require_recognised_manifest_status` (reckon/crew/promotion_checks.py:572–577), which re-raises `ManifestParseError` from `parse_manifest` while `_fresh_manifest` (same file, 462–467) swallows it as `None`; the third deliverable's refusal in `_require_*verdict_matches_exit_status` therefore fires only for a manifest that parses and genuinely records no arms
